fact_text: The P/E ratio is price divided by annual earnings per share; all else equal, a lower P/E than a peer is treated as the better value, but the price itself is set by the market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because the stock market is forward-looking, the analyst prefers forward earnings (next year's expected earnings) to trailing reported earnings when applying a P/E.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Reported earnings can differ from cash received, so a P/E built on earnings can mislead when profit is tied up in receivables or inventory, and the analyst checks for this before trusting a P/E.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Pakistan's power sector, reported profit can be far from cash because of circular debt, so earnings shown in the accounts may not be collected in cash.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Textile companies often reinvest their profits in buying higher-priced cotton for inventory, so reported earnings can carry a cash-flow problem even when profits look strong.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil marketing companies that profit when oil prices rise must buy more expensive oil next time, so their reported profit can carry a cash-flow problem.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A P/E covers finance costs but not loan principal repayments, so comparing the P/E of a heavily indebted business with a debt-free one is not a fair comparison.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For cyclical businesses the analyst uses the average earnings of the last five years instead of a single year, to smooth out the cycle before applying a P/E.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Operating margin, which is profit after all operating costs, is a better profitability measure than gross margin for comparing businesses whose overhead costs differ.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Operating margin ignores asset turnover, so a low-margin business that turns over its invested capital quickly can earn more on capital than a high-margin plant with slow turnover; read both ratios together.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Many Pakistani companies carry plants bought in the 1970s or 1980s, so the analyst restates fixed assets at replacement cost when computing ratios, to show true future profitability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cash conversion cycle is average inventory days plus average receivable days minus average payable days, measuring how long cash is tied up between buying raw materials and collecting from customers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst has rarely seen a business with heavy plant investment, a long cash conversion cycle above about 45 days, and still good returns on invested capital; asset-light businesses often run 30 to 40 days.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Apple and Amazon run negative cash conversion cycles: they collect from customers in advance and pay suppliers two to three months later.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Car, bike and tractor makers often collect customer advances, giving a negative cash cycle, but if they lack pricing power, rising raw-material costs can turn that advantage into losses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A test of pricing power is whether a company can pass a cost rise to customers; the analyst observes that car makers raise prices when the dollar rises, which shows they have pricing power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Future ROIC is future profitability divided by invested capital, where invested capital covers plant and machinery, working capital, and one-time costs such as acquiring technology.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Past ROIC does not reflect future ROIC, because future returns depend on the business's future economics, so the analyst warns against assuming a good past record will continue.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over 10 to 20 years, a stock's price growth tracks the growth in business value, so a business with 25% future ROIC would roughly multiply its value about 10 times in ten years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Warren Buffett's language, a business earning a future ROIC of 20% or more has a moat, meaning a strong position in its industry that can generate high profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For cement makers, future ROIC is easy to estimate by dividing future profit by plant cost, because working capital is small and little technology must be acquired for each plant expansion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Future ROIC for oil and gas exploration companies needs the cost of drilling a well and the success rate of finding oil, because these determine the capital needed for future profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'OUR NO.1 FINANCIAL RATIO REVEALED - HOW TO PICK  STOCKS' (YouTube transcript, undated)
